title: Llevo años diciéndolo: verbal periphrases
summary: Say how long, how often and in what spirit: llevar + gerund, seguir sin, venir diciendo, acabar por, echarse a, dar por…
focus: Verbal periphrases with the gerund, the infinitive and the participle
content:
## How long so far: llevar and seguir

- **llevar + time + gerund** = have been doing: *Llevo tres años viviendo aquí.* *¿Cuánto tiempo llevas estudiando?*
- **llevar + time + sin + infinitive** = haven't done for: *Llevo dos días sin dormir.*
- **seguir / continuar + gerund** = still be doing: *Sigue lloviendo.* **seguir sin + infinitive** = still not: *Sigo sin entenderlo.*

| | llevar | seguir |
|---|---|---|
| yo | llevo | sigo |
| tú | llevas | sigues |
| él / ella | lleva | sigue |
| nosotros | llevamos | seguimos |
| vosotros | lleváis | seguís |
| ellos | llevan | siguen |

## Gerunds with an attitude

- **ir + gerund**: little by little. *Voy entendiendo el sistema.*
- **venir + gerund**: insistently, up to now. *Te lo vengo diciendo desde enero.*
- **andar + gerund**: going around doing, often with criticism. *Anda diciendo que es el jefe.*
- **acabar + gerund**: end up. *Acabó trabajando en un banco.*

## Infinitive periphrases

| periphrasis | adds | example |
|---|---|---|
| **volver a** | again | Ha vuelto a llamar. |
| **dejar de** | stop | Dejé de fumar. |
| **ponerse a** | start (suddenly) | Se puso a llover. |
| **echarse a** | burst into (reír, llorar, correr) | Se echó a reír. |
| **llegar a** | go as far as | Llegó a pedirme dinero. |
| **acabar por** | end up | Acabé por aceptar. |
| **estar por** | be tempted to | Estoy por llamarla. |

## With the participle

- **tener + participle** stresses a result; the participle agrees with the object: *Tengo **leídas** tres novelas.*
- **llevar + participle** = so far: *Llevo **corregidos** veinte exámenes.*
- **dar por + participle** = consider: *Doy por terminada la reunión.* *Lo dimos por perdido.*
- **darle a alguien por + infinitive** = take it into one's head: *Le ha dado por correr maratones.*

vocabulary.meaning: to have been doing (+ time + gerund)
vocabulary.example: Llevamos un mes buscando piso y no hay manera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We've been looking for a flat for a month and it's hopeless.

vocabulary.meaning: to keep on, to still be (+ gerund); seguir sin = still not
vocabulary.example: Mi abuela sigue cosiendo a mano a sus noventa años.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother still sews by hand at ninety.

vocabulary.example: El enfermo va mejorando día a día.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The patient is improving day by day.

vocabulary.meaning: to have been saying (again and again)
vocabulary.example: Los vecinos vienen diciendo que el edificio necesita obras.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The neighbours have been saying for ages that the building needs work.

vocabulary.example: Anda diciendo por ahí que le van a ascender.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He's going around saying he's going to be promoted.

vocabulary.example: Tanto insistió que acabé por decirle que sí.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He insisted so much that I ended up saying yes.

vocabulary.example: No vuelvas a dejar la puerta abierta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't leave the door open again.

vocabulary.example: Por fin ha dejado de llover.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It has finally stopped raining.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto llegó, se puso a limpiar la cocina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as she arrived, she started cleaning the kitchen.

vocabulary.example: Cuando vio mi disfraz, se echó a reír.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When she saw my costume, she burst out laughing.

vocabulary.meaning: to go as far as, to manage to (+ infinitive)
vocabulary.example: Llegó a ofrecerme el doble para que me quedara.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He went as far as offering me double to stay.

vocabulary.meaning: to be tempted to, to be inclined to (+ infinitive)
vocabulary.example: Estoy por cancelar la suscripción.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm tempted to cancel the subscription.

vocabulary.meaning: to consider, to take as (+ participle)
vocabulary.example: Después de tres semanas, dieron el gato por perdido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After three weeks, they gave the cat up for lost.

vocabulary.meaning: to take it into one's head to (+ infinitive)
vocabulary.example: A mi padre le ha dado por hacer pan casero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My father has taken it into his head to make homemade bread.

conjugations.meaning: to carry; to have been (+ time + gerund)
to follow; to keep on (+ gerund)

quiz.explanation: Llevar + time + gerund says how long something has been going on: llevo tres años viviendo.
hints: The verb that also means 'to carry'.

quiz.explanation: For something you haven't done for a time: llevar + time + sin + infinitive.

quiz.prompt: ¿Todavía ___ (seguir, tú) trabajando en la misma empresa?
quiz.explanation: Seguir + gerund = still be doing. Seguir changes e to i: sigues (only yo drops the u: sigo).
hints: The e becomes i in the stressed forms.

quiz.prompt: What does 'Te lo vengo diciendo desde enero' mean?
options: I've been telling you since January (over and over).
I'm coming to tell you in January.
I told you once in January.
quiz.correct_answer: I've been telling you since January (over and over).
quiz.explanation: Venir + gerund marks an action repeated insistently up to now.
hints: Venir here is not about movement.

quiz.prompt: Al oír el chiste, todos se echaron a ___.
quiz.explanation: Echarse a takes the infinitive: echarse a reír, a llorar, a correr.
hints: After a preposition, Spanish uses the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Después de meses de dudas, Marcos ___ por aceptar el trabajo. (acabar, preterite)
quiz.explanation: Acabar por + infinitive = to end up doing something; preterite, él: acabó.

quiz.prompt: Bueno, señores, ___ por terminada la reunión.
quiz.explanation: Dar por + participle = to consider something as: doy por terminada la reunión.
In tener + participle the participle agrees with the object: tres novelas, so leídas.
hints: Feminine plural, with an accent on the í.

quiz.prompt: A mi vecino le ha dado ___ correr maratones.
quiz.explanation: Darle a alguien por + infinitive = to take it into one's head to do something.
hints: The same preposition as in dar por terminado.

listening.text: Sigue nevando en la sierra.
listening.meaning: It's still snowing in the mountains.

listening.text: Llevamos media hora esperando el autobús.
listening.meaning: We've been waiting for the bus for half an hour.

listening.text: Poco a poco voy entendiendo el sistema.
listening.meaning: Little by little I'm getting the hang of the system.

listening.text: Ha vuelto a llamar la chica del seguro.
listening.meaning: The girl from the insurance company has called again.
listening.note: New word: el seguro = the insurance.

listening.text: Dejé de fumar hace ya diez años.
listening.meaning: I stopped smoking ten years ago now.

listening.text: Anda contando a todo el mundo que se casa en mayo.
listening.meaning: She's going around telling everyone she's getting married in May.

listening.text: Estoy por mandarlo todo a paseo y mudarme al campo.
listening.meaning: I'm tempted to chuck it all in and move to the country.
listening.note: New word: mandar a paseo = to chuck in, to send packing.

listening.text: Llevo corregidos treinta exámenes y todavía me quedan otros veinte.
listening.meaning: I've marked thirty exams so far and I still have another twenty to go.

guide.tip: Gerund for something in progress (llevar, seguir, ir, venir, andar); infinitive after a preposition (volver a, dejar de, acabar por); participle for a result (tener, dar por).

conversations.title: The guitar
conversations.scenario: Sofía visits her friend Diego, who has a new hobby.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Una guitarra? ¿Desde cuándo tocas tú?
lines.meaning: A guitar? Since when do you play?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Llevo seis meses aprendiendo. Me dio por ahí en verano.
lines.meaning: I've been learning for six months. I took it into my head in the summer.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y qué tal? ¿Vas mejorando?
lines.meaning: And how's it going? Are you improving?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Poco a poco. Sigo sin saber leer partituras, eso sí.
lines.meaning: Little by little. I still can't read sheet music, mind you.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Mi hermano también se puso a tocar y acabó dejándolo.
lines.meaning: My brother also started playing and ended up giving it up.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Yo no pienso dejar de practicar. Tengo aprendidas cuatro canciones.
lines.meaning: I've no intention of giving up practising. I've learnt four songs.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Cuatro? Pues toca una, venga.
lines.meaning: Four? Go on then, play one.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, pero no te eches a reír.
lines.meaning: OK, but don't burst out laughing.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Si ni has empezado! Llevas cinco minutos afinándola.
lines.meaning: You haven't even started! You've been tuning it for five minutes.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es que vengo notando que la tercera cuerda suena rara.
lines.meaning: It's just that I've been noticing for a while that the third string sounds odd.
lines.note: venir + gerund: repeated up to now.

bites.title: Llevar + time + gerund
bites.rule: Llevo tres años viviendo aquí = I've been living here three years. With sin + infinitive: llevo dos días sin dormir.
bites.example_meaning: How long have you been waiting?

bites.title: Seguir + gerund, seguir sin
bites.rule: Sigue lloviendo = it's still raining. Sigo sin entenderlo = I still don't understand it. Seguir: sigo, sigues, sigue…

bites.title: Ir, venir, andar + gerund
bites.rule: Ir + gerund: little by little. Venir + gerund: insistently up to now. Andar + gerund: going around doing it, often a complaint.
bites.example: Anda diciendo que es el jefe.
bites.example_meaning: He goes around saying he's the boss.

bites.title: Start, stop, again, end up
bites.rule: Ponerse a / echarse a (start), dejar de (stop), volver a (again), acabar por (end up) + infinitive. Dar por + participle: consider.

sorts.title: What does it add?
sorts.why: Each periphrasis adds one shade of meaning to the main verb.

sorts.title: Gerund, infinitive or participle?
sorts.why: Gerund for an action in progress; infinitive after a preposition; participle for a result.

spots.sentence: Dejé a fumar el año pasado.
spots.why: The periphrasis is dejar de + infinitive.

spots.sentence: Tengo leído tres novelas este mes.
spots.why: With tener + participle, the participle agrees with the object.

spots.sentence: Se echó de llorar al ver la carta.
spots.why: The periphrasis is echarse a + infinitive.

builds.meaning: I've been studying Russian for two years.

builds.text: Ha vuelto a perder las llaves.

realm.content:
## Perífrasis en Eldmark

The hunter **lleva** tres días **siguiendo** el rastro del grifo; the bard **anda contando** que lo cazará él solo. The mage **sigue sin encontrar** el hechizo correcto, and the ring? **Lo dimos por perdido** hasta que el enano **se puso a cavar** y **volvió a** aparecer.

vocabulary.example: El cazador lleva tres días siguiendo el rastro del grifo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hunter has been following the griffin's trail for three days.

vocabulary.example: La maga sigue sin encontrar el hechizo correcto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage still hasn't found the right spell.

vocabulary.example: El bardo anda diciendo que cazará el grifo él solo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The bard goes around saying he'll hunt the griffin on his own.

vocabulary.example: Dimos el anillo por perdido en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We gave the ring up for lost in the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: El enano se puso a cavar y encontró oro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf started digging and found gold.

vocabulary.example: El grifo volvió a escaparse.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The griffin escaped again.

vocabulary.example: El bardo no deja de cantar ni un minuto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The bard doesn't stop singing for a minute.

vocabulary.example: Lleva toda la mañana tensando el arco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He's been stringing the bow all morning.

bites.title: Tres días tras el grifo
bites.rule: Llevar + time + gerund for a long hunt, seguir sin for what hasn't happened yet, volver a for what happens again.
bites.example: Llevamos tres días siguiendo al grifo.
bites.example_meaning: We've been following the griffin for three days.

listening.text: Llevamos tres días siguiendo al grifo.
listening.meaning: We've been following the griffin for three days.
listening.note: New word: el grifo = the griffin.

listening.text: El cazador sigue sin ver al grifo.
listening.meaning: The hunter still hasn't seen the griffin.

listening.text: El bardo no deja de cantar.
listening.meaning: The bard doesn't stop singing.
listening.note: New word: el bardo = the bard.

listening.text: El orco se echó a correr.
listening.meaning: The orc broke into a run.

listening.text: Dimos el anillo por perdido.
listening.meaning: We gave the ring up for lost.

builds.text: La maga sigue sin encontrar el hechizo.
builds.meaning: The mage still hasn't found the spell.

spots.sentence: El cazador lleva tres días seguir el rastro.
El bardo no deja a cantar.

sorts.title: ¿Qué añade?

items.text: El enano se puso a cavar.
El orco se echó a correr.

sorts.why: Ponerse a / echarse a start an action, dejar de stops it, volver a repeats it.

quiz.prompt: El cazador ___ tres días siguiendo el rastro del grifo. (present)
quiz.explanation: Llevar + time + gerund: lleva tres días siguiendo.

quiz.prompt: El bardo ___ diciendo que cazará el grifo él solo.
quiz.explanation: Andar + gerund = going around doing something, often with a critical tone.

meadowbrook.content:
## Perífrasis en Meadowbrook

Nora **lleva** dos años **cultivando** fresas and **sigue sin** tener tractor. Poco a poco el maíz **va creciendo**. The mayor **vuelve a** dar discursos, Leo **anda diciendo** que pescó un pez de un metro, and the new goat **acabó comiéndose** el sombrero de Rosa.

vocabulary.example: Nora lleva dos años cultivando fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora has been growing strawberries for two years.

vocabulary.example: Sigo sin tener tractor, así que aro a mano.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I still don't have a tractor, so I plough by hand.

vocabulary.example: Con la lluvia, el huerto va mejorando.
vocabulary.example_meaning: With the rain, the vegetable garden is improving.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde ha vuelto a dar un discurso eterno.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor has given an endless speech again.

vocabulary.example: Leo anda diciendo que pescó un pez de un metro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo is going around saying he caught a one-metre fish.

vocabulary.example: Rosa lleva años cultivando tomates raros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa has been growing unusual tomatoes for years.

vocabulary.example: El tractor viejo ha vuelto a romperse.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The old tractor has broken down again.

vocabulary.example: La cabra acabó comiéndose el sombrero de Rosa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The goat ended up eating Rosa's hat.

bites.title: Poco a poco en la granja
bites.rule: Farm life is gradual: lleva dos años cultivando, va creciendo, sigue sin llover. And things keep happening again: vuelve a romperse.

listening.text: El maíz va creciendo poco a poco.
listening.meaning: The maize is growing little by little.

listening.text: Lleva dos años cultivando fresas.
listening.meaning: She's been growing strawberries for two years.

listening.text: El tractor de Leo volvió a fallar.
listening.meaning: Leo's tractor broke down again.
listening.note: New word: el tractor = the tractor.

listening.text: La cabra acabó comiéndose el sombrero.
listening.meaning: The goat ate the hat.

listening.text: Sigue sin llover en el valle.
listening.meaning: It still hasn't rained in the valley.

builds.meaning: I've been growing strawberries for two years.

builds.text: El tractor ha vuelto a romperse.
builds.meaning: The tractor has broken down again.

spots.sentence: Sigue sin lloviendo en el valle.
Nora lleva dos años cultivar fresas.

sorts.title: ¿Gerundio o infinitivo?
sorts.why: Ir, llevar and andar take the gerund; volver a, dejar de and seguir sin take the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: El tractor viejo ha vuelto ___ romperse.

conversations.title: The old tractor
conversations.scenario: Leo the fisherman finds Nora the farmer next to her broken tractor.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Otra vez el tractor? ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas arreglándolo?
lines.meaning: The tractor again? How long have you been fixing it?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Llevo toda la mañana, y sigue sin arrancar.
lines.meaning: All morning, and it still won't start.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te lo vengo diciendo desde la primavera: necesitas uno nuevo.
lines.meaning: I've been telling you since spring: you need a new one.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ya, pero si dejo de ahorrar, no compro las semillas.
lines.meaning: I know, but if I stop saving, I can't buy the seeds.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues acabarás arando a mano, como tu abuela.
lines.meaning: Then you'll end up ploughing by hand, like your grandmother.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Estoy por venderlo al alcalde para su museo.
lines.meaning: I'm tempted to sell it to the mayor for his museum.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Su museo? Le ha dado por coleccionar cosas viejas.
lines.meaning: His museum? He's taken it into his head to collect old things.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Mira! Ha vuelto a arrancar.
lines.meaning: Look! It's started again.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Doy por perdida la apuesta, entonces.
lines.meaning: I'll consider the bet lost, then.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me debes un pescado, Leo.
lines.meaning: You owe me a fish, Leo.

rustwake.content:
## Perífrasis en el páramo

I **llevo** semanas **reparando** el robot jardinero and it **sigue sin arrancar**. One day I **me puse a desmontar** the motor and found a beetle inside. The beetle **se echó a correr**, the robot **volvió a** funcionar, and Leo **anda contando** que fue idea suya.

vocabulary.example: Llevo semanas reparando el robot jardinero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I've been repairing the gardener robot for weeks.

vocabulary.example: El robot sigue sin arrancar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The robot still won't start.

vocabulary.example: Me puse a desmontar el motor con una cuchara.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I started taking the engine apart with a spoon.

vocabulary.example: Por fin el robot volvió a funcionar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: At last the robot worked again.

vocabulary.example: Estoy por cambiar el robot por cien tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm tempted to swap the robot for a hundred nuts.

vocabulary.example: El camión lleva un mes sin arrancar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The truck hasn't started for a month.

vocabulary.example: No vuelvas a desmontar mi radiorreloj.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't take my wrist radio apart again.

vocabulary.example: Sigo buscando la pieza que falta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm still looking for the missing part.

bites.title: Semanas en el taller
bites.rule: Workshop life: llevo semanas reparando, sigue sin arrancar, me puse a desmontar, volvió a funcionar.

listening.text: Llevo dos días buscando pilas.
listening.meaning: I've been looking for batteries for two days.

listening.text: El camión sigue sin arrancar.
listening.meaning: The truck still won't start.
listening.note: New word: arrancar = to start (an engine).

listening.text: Me puse a desmontar el motor.
listening.meaning: I started taking the engine apart.
listening.note: New word: desmontar = to take apart.

listening.text: El escarabajo se echó a correr.
listening.meaning: The beetle broke into a run.

listening.text: Sigo sin encontrar la última pieza.
listening.meaning: I still haven't found the last part.
listening.note: New word: la pieza = the part.

builds.meaning: I've been repairing the robot for weeks.

spots.sentence: Me puse de desmontar el motor.

sorts.title: ¿Cuánto tiempo, todavía o de nuevo?
sorts.why: Llevar measures time, seguir says it is still the case, volver a says it happens again.

quiz.explanation: Seguir sin + infinitive = still not; él: sigue.
hints: The e becomes i, and gu appears before e.

quiz.explanation: Ponerse a + infinitive = to start doing something.
hints: The same preposition as volver a.
